Feature generation step uses an LLM to create multiple new feature transformation programs leveraging prior knowledge, reasoning, and in-context learning to explore feature space (Figure 1(a)).
Structured prompting methodology developed to facilitate effective and contextually relevant feature discovery programs.

Prompt designed to provide: comprehensive data-specific information, initial feature transformation program as evolution starting point, evaluation function, and well-defined output format (Appendix B.1).
LLM instruction assigns the task of finding the most relevant features to solve given task, emphasizing prior knowledge of dataset domain.
LLM explicitly instructed to generate novel features and provide clear step-by-step reasoning for prediction task relevance.
LLM specifically instructed to generate complex features because LLMs tend to generate simple features.
Dataset specification presents LLM with metadata M: detailed task description, feature names C, and corresponding descriptions.

Limited number of representative tabular samples provided, serialized as Serialize(xi, yi, C) = 'If c1 is x1 i, ..., cd is xd i. Then Result is yi' (Eq. 3), following Dinh et al. (2022), Hegselmann et al. (2023), Han et al. (2024).
Dataset-specific details guide LLM to focus on contextually pertinent features supporting dataset and task objective.
Evaluation function incorporated in prompt guides LLM to generate feature transformation programs aligning with performance objectives.
Programs augment original dataset with new features, evaluated via prediction model performance on augmented data; validation score serves as quality indicator.
Including evaluation function ensures LLM programs are inherently aligned with performance criteria.
In-context demonstration samples k highest-performing demonstrations from previous iterations for LLM to build on successful outputs.
Iterative interaction between LLM outputs and evaluator feedback facilitates systematic refinement, progressively improving outputs using patterns and insights from prior demonstrations.
Feature sampling at iteration t constructs prompt pt from previous iteration to LLM pi_theta, sampling b programs: T1, ..., Tb = pi_theta(pt).
Stochastic temperature-based sampling employed to promote diversity and balance exploration (creativity) vs exploitation (prior knowledge).
Each sampled feature transform Ti executed prior to evaluation to discard error-prone programs, ensuring only valid executable programs enter optimization pipeline.
Computational efficiency maintained by enforcing maximum execution time threshold, discarding any program exceeding it.
